title: A tiny load accumulates
hook: Two watts over a whole day and over one hour are different annual totals.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert a small stated constant load into a multiday energy quantity.

misconception: A small wattage cannot accumulate a meaningful quantity over many days.
objective: Convert a small stated constant load into a multiday energy quantity.

claims.text: A constant illustrative 2W load runs for either 24h/day or 1h/day. Scaled model; illustrative:2W;24h/day-or-1h/day;€0.30/kWh.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Days=365, A=17.52kWh and B=0.73kWh. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",2,24,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",2,"x"],1000]; x denotes Days. At x=365, A=17.52, B=0.73. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A daily amount repeats across days. The formula multiplies watts, hours per day, and days before dividing by one thousand. It describes a hypothetical constant load and does not instruct you to disconnect safety-critical equipment.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/",["*",2,24,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",2,"x"],1000]; x denotes Days. At x=365, A=17.52, B=0.73. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: An illustrative constant 3W load runs 24 hours a day for 365 days. About how much energy does it accumulate? Correct: 26.3kWh. 3W × 24h × 365 days = 26,280Wh, about 26.3kWh: a small daily amount repeats every day.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Same as lh-fixed-energy-charge c5: this is the unit definition (kWh = W × h ÷ 1000) and the model's arithmetic. formulaA = 2 × 24 × x ÷ 1000 and formulaB = 2 × x ÷ 1000; own run of resource-model.ts at 365 days gives 17.52 kWh and 0.73 kWh. Price × kWh appears in the assumptions (€0.30/kWh). Verified on the definition; energy.gov.au was not opened and is not relied on.
